body_text:
v0.22.0: Brick by brick

An interactive fiction with RPG and management elements where you build your own criminal empire. You take on the role of a girl raised in a crime dynasty, sent on a mission to establish her own organization in a city flooded with gangs. Choose your bio - and go, commit some crimes. You start as a no-name hustler who just moved into the city, and you gotta make a name for yourself. Steal cars, rob houses, pick pockets, distribute and cook various substances ghetto-style or get yourself a nice cozy lab, and a lot more. And soon enough, you're gonna conquer all the turfs and set up a bunch of shady enterprises.

Do not forget to check the credits[1]. There you'll find the download link for desktop version, attributions, changelogs, Patreon link, and all the necessary contact information if such a need arises.

body_text:
- "Burglary, huh? Well, you can keep the tools we found on you. But nothing else."
The other agent leans forward, his tone sharper now. - "So, about our warning, you're going to thaaat city, y'know, Ambush Alley."

They pause for a moment, letting the weight of the name sink in. Everything that you know about this city is that its full of gangs, power struggles, and violence, and has no real order. Tortuga of modern world. Your father was talking about it with his partners in crime, and, if you remember correctly, they wanted to add it to their empire. So, it is how he decided to do it...?

- "Have you heard about a huge police crackdown that happened three months ago in Ambush Alley?" - one of the agents broke the silence. You shook your head. - "Basically, one raid changed everything. Gangs were fractured, businesses shut down, prison cells are overflowing. This is a free real estate right now. And someone from your family, you know, someone who SAVES you all the time, wants you to prove yourself. And he says that you're ready for that. But i'll be honest, odds are against you." - He pauses, giving you a pointed look.

- "And now, you’re going to be thrown into that mess. Your job? Setup your own gang in Ambush Alley. Restore some kind of control. Or at least the money flow. The methods are up to you. No one will judge, do whatever it takes. We'll assist you if you get yourself in trouble, police chief of Ambush Alley is our guy. And you'll getting yourself your very own apartments... in a basement. Any questions?"

Other gangs?[1]
How can i get some money?[2]
How do i organize my own gang?[3]
What do you recommend me to do first?[4]

No questions.[5]

You were transported to the outskirts of the city through a variety of routes, each more discrete than the last. The agents made sure to keep their distance, ensuring no one followed you. By the time you reached the border of the city, the car you were in had already passed through several police checkpoints.

The car stopped in front of an unremarkable house. The agents let the engine idle for a moment, then one of them turned to you with a stern expression.

- "This is it. You’ll find your place here for now. Keep a low profile. And don’t forget about the whiteboard inside the house - it’s important. If you need any more advices - use a red phone, it should be somewhere in the house."

You nodded, the weight of the situation settling in as the door was opened for you. With one last look at the agents, you stepped out into the crumbling neighborhood. The city loomed ahead, still a chaotic mess, but now, it was yours to control.

The outskirts of Ambush Alley are dotted with trailers and farming plots. Trucks loaded with goods frequently race down the roads, adding a constant hum of activity to the otherwise quiet surroundings. Most likely, all these trucks are paying their dues to you.

 Visit "The Fringe" club.[1] 
Buy an abandoned workshop for 70000$ and setup a chemistry lab.
 Hop into the Junkyard.[2] 
 Visit the local checkpoint.[3] It's under Bikers control. 
Wait for the night if you wanna try a car theft. Don't forget your tools.
A racetrack winds around the entire outskirts, and nearby posters are advertising nightly races starting at 8 PM.
Local farmers set up a market nearby. You could buy some agricultural produce from them at a bargain price.
Check their offers.[4]

 Get back home[5]
 Open map[6]

v0.22.0: Brick by brick

An interactive fiction with RPG and management elements where you build your own criminal empire. You take on the role of a girl raised in a crime dynasty, sent on a mission to establish her own organization in a city flooded with gangs. Choose your bio - and go, commit some crimes. You start as a no-name hustler who just moved into the city, and you gotta make a name for yourself. Steal cars, rob houses, pick pockets, distribute and cook various substances ghetto-style or get yourself a nice cozy lab, and a lot more. And soon enough, you're gonna conquer all the turfs and set up a bunch of shady enterprises.

Do not forget to check the credits[1]. There you'll find the download link for desktop version, attributions, changelogs, Patreon link, and all the necessary contact information if such a need arises.

You find yourself once again in the interrogation room with the two federal agents. They've got that tired look on their faces, well, of course, you've been here before.

- "Well, here we are again," one of the agents sighs, rubbing his forehead. "You manage to get yourself caught, and now we have to bail you out... again. But this time, it’s different."

You raised an eyebrow in surprise.

- "We'll get to it in no time. Let's do a rundown on your criminal records first, you know, usual stuff." the second agent pulls out a thick folder from the stack of papers on the table, flipping it open with a slight rustle. He looks at the pages for a moment, eyes scanning the text, before giving you a knowing glance. "Here we go. Your history's all laid out. Correct me if i'm wrong."

You raised an eyebrow in surprise.

body_text:
- "Burglary, huh? Well, you can keep the tools we found on you. But nothing else."
The other agent leans forward, his tone sharper now. - "So, about our warning, you're going to thaaat city, y'know, Kickback Keys."

They pause for a moment, letting the weight of the name sink in. Everything that you know about this city is that its full of gangs, power struggles, and violence, and has no real order. Tortuga of modern world. Your father was talking about it with his partners in crime, and, if you remember correctly, they wanted to add it to their empire. So, it is how he decided to do it...?

- "Have you heard about a huge police crackdown that happened three months ago in Kickback Keys?" - one of the agents broke the silence. You shook your head. - "Basically, one raid changed everything. Gangs were fractured, businesses shut down, prison cells are overflowing. This is a free real estate right now. And someone from your family, you know, someone who SAVES you all the time, wants you to prove yourself. And he says that you're ready for that. But i'll be honest, odds are against you." - He pauses, giving you a pointed look.

- "And now, you’re going to be thrown into that mess. Your job? Setup your own gang in Kickback Keys. Restore some kind of control. Or at least the money flow. The methods are up to you. No one will judge, do whatever it takes. We'll assist you if you get yourself in trouble, police chief of Kickback Keys is our guy. And you'll getting yourself your very own apartments... in a basement. Any questions?"

Other gangs?[1]
How can i get some money?[2]
How do i organize my own gang?[3]
What do you recommend me to do first?[4]

No questions.[5]

body_text:
You were transported to the outskirts of the city through a variety of routes, each more discrete than the last. The agents made sure to keep their distance, ensuring no one followed you. By the time you reached the border of the city, the car you were in had already passed through several police checkpoints.

The car stopped in front of an unremarkable house. The agents let the engine idle for a moment, then one of them turned to you with a stern expression.

- "This is it. You’ll find your place here for now. Keep a low profile. And don’t forget about the whiteboard inside the house - it’s important. If you need any more advices - use a red phone, it should be somewhere in the house."

You nodded, the weight of the situation settling in as the door was opened for you. With one last look at the agents, you stepped out into the crumbling neighborhood. The city loomed ahead, still a chaotic mess, but now, it was yours to control.

You're in Old Downtown of Kickback Keys. Despite the name, this part of the city is far from a business hub, previously it was a city center, now its almost a ghetto. However, it hosts the majority of businesses, along with sprawling residential areas and housing projects, making it easier to maintain control here than in quieter districts. The people from these areas currently hold control over this district.

Go to the marketplace.[1]
Visit the bar "The Underworld Lounge".[2]
Visit the "Instant Worth Pawn" pawnshop.[3]
Visit the "Wild Rabbit" Sexshop.[4]
Stride to the Nightclub "The Getaway Groove".[5]
You don't know a location of Street Gangs hub. You should ask people around if you wish to find it.
Check the local stroll.[6] It's under Street Gangs control.
You may use your lockpick[7] to try yourself in burglary craft in local residential complex.

Get back home[8]

To establish your own "organization," you need to achieve the following goals:

1. More than 10000$ in the account.


2. Own a warehouse. You won't get far without it. Huge boost to your earning and rep. The warehouse district is located at the harbor.


3. Own a house. You need your own HQ as a base of operations. You can look for a new house by browsing on your PC.


4. Locate and get acquainted with all the major forces in the city: the mafia, cartels, gangs, and bikers. Visit all the districts and search around; you’ll eventually find everything you need. Or... work on your rep, they'll contact you anyway.


5. Achieve the reputation of a 'Big Shot' - people need to know your name. Just do your thing. Anything related to criminal activity will give your reputation a solid boost.


6. Have at least three handguns ("Block 19") at your disposal. It's better to be prepared for any consequences. If you can't find any guns, buy them from local gun dealers. Rumor has it that bikers are selling weapons without any traces.


7. Achieve a gang strength value above 300. You might not have your own organization just yet, but it never hurts to prepare your future crew. ) - that’s what marks them as potential recruits. Higher their combat - more strength they give.

body_text:
The Fringe Club - a fitting name for an "offbeat" venue tucked away on the outskirts of the city. The place exudes grit, with leather-clad patrons and a parking lot packed with bikes and pickup trucks. Even before stepping inside the occasional burst of laughter hint at the atmosphere. You’d expect your arrival to turn heads, but as you walk in, the crowd barely spares you a glance, each engrossed in their own world.

Ask around about biker's leader.[1]

 Go back outside.[2]

With the right setup, you could build an improvised weapons workshop here. Buyout price: 50000$. Daily maintenance costs: 170$/day.
You need to establish a gang first.

You're too tired for scavenging.

 Get back to home[1]

 Visit "The Fringe" club.[1]

body_text:
A badly lit room filled with the smell of smoke and the sound of low, thumping music. The walls are adorned with graffiti, and a couple of neon signs flicker intermittently. Yeah, that's obviously a gang's nest. You steps into the room, where three figures are seated.
Biggest (and blackest) figurine looks up to you lazily from his spot on the sofa, his eyes half-closed, yet sharp.


- "Ayo, ayo… look who decided to pull up. Heard the chatter ‘bout you. Name’s Biggie. I keep things vibin’ around here, no cap. Downtown’s our spot, and if you tryna play in our sandbox, you best not mess up anythin' or it'll be minus vibe, feel me?"

The second guy, who had been lounging in a chair and playing with a knife, fixed his gaze on you.


- "Yeah, yeah, I’m Slick Trick. Don’t think I don’t know what you’re about. We got ears everywhere, see? You got somethin’ goin' on, you come to us first. No questions asked. Otherwise..." - He flips the knife, catching it by the blade, grinning. - "...things might get... tricky."



The third guy nods absentmindedly, taking a long drag from whatever he’s smoking. He leans back, eyes half-closed, exhaling a cloud of smoke.
-"And this here’s Sub-Dizzy. Dude’s not a talker, but trust, he’s got the 411 on all the street biz. If Dizzy ain't feelin’ you, we ain’t feelin’ you, sis. You get it?"

Biggie chuckles softly - "Look, we ain't some boomer-heads, ya feel? You keep it chill with us, we keep it chill with you. It's that simple. Don’t be doin' no wild shit on our block, and Biggie ain’t even gonna move from this couch, fam. Plus, if you pull together your own crew, we can hook you up with the local vibes - you know, get the lowkey contacts for the shorties and maybe help you score some… stuff, if you catch my drift. For a price, of course."

 Got it.

body_text:
You walk into a lavish, dimly lit room. A large mahogany desk sits at the center, and behind it, lounging in a leather chair, is the mafia leader. He's impeccably dressed in a tailored suit, a smirk playing on his lips as he shuffles a deck of cards.

- "Ah, finalmente! The new hustler I've been hearing about. Benvenuta! I've been waiting for the chance to meet the lady who runs these streets like they're her personal racetrack. My name is Alfa Romano, nice to meet you!"
He gestures you to sit in the chair opposite him, his eyes glinting with interest.
- "Please, make yourself at home. Mi chiamo vincenzo. I like a woman who knows her way around a job, capisce? And I've got a feeling you're gonna like what I have to offer. See, I've got a little... operation. Cars, mostly. We find 'em, we take 'em, we make 'em disappear, and voilà! They come back with a whole new identity."
He leans back, casually tossing the cards from one hand to the other.
- "But I ain't just about cars, you know. Io amo il gioco! I love the thrill of a good gamble. It's why I'm in the business of buying those casino crowns. You bring me your crowns, I pay you double in cash. In dirty cash, if you know what i mean. No questions asked. And if you're feeling lucky, maybe you and I can play a little blackjack sometime. I'm always up for a good game. So, cara mia, what do you say? You scratch my back, I scratch yours."

 Got it.

body_text:
You've asked a few bikers about their leader and they very easily helped you to locate him.
He's standing at the corner of the bar. A hulking figure with a weathered leather jacket and a cigar hanging from his lips. His eyes flick to you as you approach, sharp and calculating.

He takes a slow puff, then nods slightly, motioning for you to sit. "Volkov," he says simply, his accent thick, voice gravelly. He taps his chest with two fingers, then points at you. "You?"
You introduce yourself, and he nods again, seemingly satisfied. He leans in, lowering his voice. "Business?" His eyes gleam at the word.
- "You got money? Dirty?" he asks, leaning back. "I clean. Three for one." He holds up three fingers, then one, to make sure you understand.
He takes a sip from his glass, never taking his eyes off you. "You got cargo?" He makes a plane gesture with his hand, tilting it back and forth. "I ship. Big reward. At the local landing strip." His grin is quick, almost feral. "You bring cash. I bring... solution. And i can help with heat... By doing distraction. Once a week. For 8000$ in clean. If someone's gonna vote for you. Understand?"
He leans back, giving a small, almost indifferent shrug. "No cash, no talk." He points to his pocket, then to you. "Money... speaks."

 Right.

body_text: Heisting[1]
body_html:
Heisting[1]
Your daily progress in heist preparation depends on your cunning and various bonuses from your Street Gang.
Potential heist preparation progress: 6 pts.
All operations have to be launched between 08:00 and 23:00.
Heist Crew[2]
► Five-finger Discount
Crime: Robbery
Legal code: Article 212. Unlawful taking of property through force, threat, or intimidation, weapon or not.
Sentence: 3-7 years in prison
Info: A fast grab behind the counter while the clerk is distracted. You take the cash, your partner keeps the clerk busy. Low payout, low profile. Sometimes small jobs are enough to keep things running.
Intel required: 75 pts
Preparation cost: 1500$
Potential score: 0-15000$
Crew: Thief
Risks: Low to medium. Getting caught is not just prison time. The clerk might hit the panic button and local cops are quick to respond. High cunning for both the Boss and the thief increases the time window and reduces mistakes.
Possible heat: 12-25%
Equipment: None required. A hoodie and a cheap mask probably?
Special conditions: None
Not enough money.
► Cash on the Wheels
Crime: Armed Robbery
Legal code: Article 215. Armed robbery involving force or intimidation while carrying a dangerous weapon or its imitation.
Sentence: 15-25 years in prison
Info: A planned road ambush on a cash-in-transit van. You study the full route and pick the right place to strike. Timing, traffic and guard behavior matter. Cash collectors are armed and trained. Push too hard and they will shoot. Push just right and they might choose life over duty.
Intel required: 135 pts
Preparation cost: 10000$
Potential score: 50000-150000$
Crew: Driver, Main Gunner
Risks: Medium. Armed guards, unpredictable reactions, and a real chance of a shootout. The Boss must be ready to intimidate or pull the trigger if negotiations fail.
Possible heat: 60-80%
Equipment: 1 I16 and 1 Block 19, both kept. 1 van, disposable.
Special conditions: Route intel from a friendly banker.
Not enough money.
► Gather the Materials
Crime: Grand Larceny
Legal code: Article 189. Theft of property valued at 10000$ or more from a warehouse or distribution facility with intent to permanently deprive the owner.
Sentence: 10-20 years in prison
Info: A full-scale warehouse robbery. Not some random harbor storage, but Cartel property. You are not after common goods and you are not leaving leftovers behind. The official sentence is meaningless here. Failure means consequences far beyond prison.
Intel required: 175 pts
Preparation cost: 15000$
Potential score: Large quantities of various materials
Crew: Driver, Thief
Risks: Medium to high. Expect serious physical work from the thief. The Boss provides support and problem solving with sharp cunning. Cartel guards are not forgiving.
Possible heat: 40-50%
Equipment: 1 van, disposable. 10 lockpicks, consumed during the job.
Special conditions: Personal scouting of Cartel warehouses may open alternative approaches or distractions.
Not enough money.
► Funny Papers
Crime: Tax Evasion
Legal code: Article 312. Willful evasion of tax assessment, reporting, or payment through fraud, misrepresentation, or concealed finances.
Sentence: 25 years to life
Info: This is not a smash-and-grab. It is paperwork, lies, and creative accounting. Shell companies, fake invoices, offshore transfers. Everyone in your gang plays a part. The goal is to make everything look legitimate just long enough to cash out before auditors connect the dots.
Intel required: 200 pts
Preparation cost: 20000$
Potential score: ~1000-5000$ per gang member
Crew: Driver, Main Gunner
Risks: High. You can lose everything invested. Worse, the IRS may start digging if this operation fails.
Possible heat: 40-60%
Equipment: A quick mind and 10 stacks of paperwork.
Special conditions: Having a friendly taxman willing to take the fall can soften the consequences.
Not enough money.
► The Cage Job
Crime: Casino Heist
Legal code: Article 178, criminal conspiracy. Article 215, armed robbery involving force or intimidation with a weapon.
Sentence: 25 years to life, stacked counts likely
Info: A full scale hit on the casino cage and vault. The Driver keeps timing tight and exits clean. The Safecracker handles doors, systems, and finesse. The Main Gunner controls pressure when things spike. The Boss must rely on sharp cunning. Breach security, neutralize guards, clear the vault. Good coordination means fewer mistakes and more time inside the cage.
Intel required: 300 pts. Has an additional means of intel boost.
Preparation cost: 40000$
Potential score: 100000-300000$ plus casino tokens and vault valuables
Crew: Driver, Safecracker, Main Gunner
Risks: High. Silent alarms, overlapping cameras, panic buttons everywhere. Coordination errors directly reduce vault time.
Possible heat: 50-80%
Equipment: 1 van, disposable. 10 lockpicks, consumed. 1 I16 and 4 Block 19s, disposable.
Additional requirement: 6000 gang strength.
Special conditions: There may be a cleaner approach than brute force. Building plans show a VIP guest room with a ventilation shaft leading to the security booth. Those rooms are booked months ahead and breaking in is a job on its own, so direct access is unrealistic. Still, infiltrating guest rooms may provide valuable intel.
Your gang isn't big enough to take such risks.
► The Long Count
Crime: Bank Robbery
Legal code: Armed robbery, hostage taking, criminal conspiracy.
Sentence: 25 years to life, multiple stacked counts
Info: A full takeover of a working bank during operating hours. This is not a quick hit. You lock the doors, control the floor, and turn civilians into leverage. While the Safecracker works the vault, the Boss handles negotiations, pressure, and damage control. The Main Gunner keeps order when nerves break. The Driver keeps engines warm and timing precise. Every mistake shortens your window. This job is about control, not speed. Also, better close your credits before doing this, it'll send bank building on maintenance for sure.
Intel required: 400 pts
Preparation cost: 75000$
Potential score: 100000-1000000$ depending on execution, negotiation outcomes, and vault clear
Crew: Driver, Safecracker, Main Gunner
Risks: Extreme. Armed response, tactical units, snipers, and media pressure. Hostages can panic, resist, or turn into liabilities. Poor negotiation or excessive violence rapidly escalates the situation and cuts into vault time.
Possible heat: 80-99%
Equipment: 1 van. 3 I16 rifles. 3 Block 19.
Additional requirement: 5000 gang strength.
Special conditions: Police connections can delay first responders and buy crucial minutes. A friendly banker may provide intel on staffing schedules, and the best moment to strike. Both advantages reduce early pressure but will not stop the final response.
Your gang isn't big enough to take such risks.

The gang gathers around the table, stacks of documents spread out like a damn battlefield map, every piece of the puzzle laid bare. Plans are whispered, numbers are crunched, and loopholes are carefully threaded. It’s not just about hiding the money, it’s about making it disappear without a trace...

Hours have slipped away in a haze of numbers and fine print. The groundwork is done, but now comes the trickiest part - the final touches. One last adjustment, one last forged signature, one last transaction to tie it all together. The clock is ticking, and the post office is about to close. If the documents aren’t sent out in time, the whole scheme falls apart. You need to finish it, personally, as a boss.

Hints for tax evasion.[1]And remember, for every second you're rushing you're losing time.
Let's begin.[2]

body_text:
You push open the door of a dingy office with faded “404 Bleach” lettering half-peeled from the window. A bell jingles weakly. A man looks up from behind a desk stacked with paperwork and empty coffee cups. Classic rundown scenery.
- "We’re closed. Try someplace else."
You explain that Chi Eef sent you, and you're here to offload some heat.
- "Ah. You one of that kind. Should've guessed."
He quickly raises his eyes, squinting at you through smudged glasses. He adjusts a crooked nameplate that says nothing.
- "Name’s Mr. Scrubbs. Ain’t on any paperwork, but around here names don’t clean much anyway. Place went to hell after the last big raid. Cops hit half the city’s shadows - we lost clients, crew, cover... everything but the dust."
He lets out a dry chuckle, then wipes his hands on an old towel that looks dirtier than his desk.
- "My last girl walked out two days ago. Said even pretending to mop bloodstains wasn’t worth the risk anymore. So yeah, I know why you're here. But I can't help much... unless you're looking to take a job yourself. If so - I might still have a mop and a mess for you."
You shrug, as if dirty work’s just another Tuesday for you. He quickly glanced over his papers:
- "But-but, I guess you're aiming higher than just being a fake maid, if you came here because of heat? Then there’s only one rule — you don’t work here more than once every few days. Familiar faces get remembered, and around here, memory gets people in trouble."

Nod.

body_text:
The hooded guy leans against the doorway of the dimly lit hideout, his silhouette outlined by the flickering glow of monitors and the hum of electronics.

- "So, you were looking for our place. Name's Sixth. Yeah, just Sixth. The rest of my crew, well, they prefer to stay in the shadows. Let's just say I'm the friendly face of our little operation."
He steps aside, gesturing for the player to enter, before continuing.
- "We run a tight ship here, all about information and electronics. You need intel on a juicy target? We can hook you up. But, it's a two-way street. We’re always in the market for certain...components. The kind that don’t have serial numbers. If you happen to come across anything of interest, we might be able to make a deal. Help us out enough, and maybe, just maybe, we’ll show you a trick or two that could make your life a whole lot easier."

 Nod.
